text:
Alex Ovechkin arrived in Ottawa this week to a planned protest over his support for Vladimir Putin, which CBC, The Globe and Mail and RMNB all covered. He was also asked about Canada blocking Russia's return to the World Juniors and said Russian athletes want to represent their country, declining to weigh in on the Court of Arbitration for Sport decision. One headline carried his response to the protest: "Nobody's Using Me." His ties to Putin have followed him for years; this week they were the story.

On the ice, the NHL's career goals leader, who passed Wayne Gretzky in April 2025, has one goal in 16 games and none in eleven. He is 41, playing under 14 minutes a night, with no power-play points.

The chances are still coming. He has 4.66 individual expected goals and is shooting 3.8% against a usual range near 12.5%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 94th percentile for chances from the home plate last season. Washington is a little better in chance share with him on the ice. Our numbers say the goals should come; the question is how long his minutes hold if they don't.
headline: Ovechkin's season: one goal, and a protest in Ottawa
